name: Apple M4 Pro (MacBook Pro 14-inch, 2024)
memory_bandwidth_basis: Apple tech specs: '273GB/s memory bandwidth' for the M4 Pro with 12-core CPU / 16-core GPU; configurable to M4 Pro with 14-core CPU / 20-core GPU at the same 273GB/s. Unified-memory bandwidth, package-level, shared with the CPU.
notes:
M4 Pro: 16-core or 20-core GPU, 16-core Neural Engine, up to 48GB unified memory. The 273GB/s bandwidth is the base configuration; the M4 Max at 410GB/s or 546GB/s is the higher-bandwidth option. For local LLM inference, the 48GB unified pool can hold a 70B model at 4-bit (~35GB weights) with room for KV cache, but the 273GB/s bandwidth limits decode speed to roughly 8-12 tokens/sec for a 70B model. The M4 Pro is the entry point for serious local LLM work on Apple Silicon.
MEMORY_BUS_WIDTH: STILL NULL, AND HERE IS PRECISELY WHAT WAS LOOKED FOR (2026-10-04). %s NO FIGURE WAS BACK-COMPUTED FROM BANDWIDTH. That is the standing rule for this field in this repo and it was applied to every null here rather than to a subset: a width derived by dividing a published aggregate bandwidth by an assumed or half-assumed per-pin rate is two inferences stacked on one number, and if either inference is wrong the record looks populated while being wrong. The correct state of this field is 'the vendor does not publish it', and the note above names the specific document that was read and found not to carry it, so a future pass does not have to re-establish that from scratch.

MEMORY_BUS_WIDTH: STILL NULL, AND HERE IS PRECISELY WHAT WAS LOOKED FOR (2026-10-04). Apple's own tech-specs pages publish MEMORY BANDWIDTH ONLY and have never published a memory-bus width in bits for any M-series part. Verified directly this pass on support.apple.com/en-us/111900 (Mac Studio 2022) and /en-us/122211 (Mac Studio 2025), which carry '400GB/s', '800GB/s', '410GB/s', '546GB/s' and '819GB/s' rows and no width row at all. Not back-computed: the published figures are per-SoC aggregates across a multi-package design and LPDDR5X runs at several pin rates depending on SKU, so no single width reconciles them all.
